sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 6:19

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 6:19:1
items.html:
He looks at those lights of AHP, etc., for the need of making the vessels of the Nekudot: Behold, the ARI speaks here of the discernment of the ten Sefirot of the hairs. For you already know that because of the ascent of the bottom Hey to the Nikvey Einayim, the Rosh [head] of SAG was immediately divided into two discernments, Rosh and Guf [body]: GE remained as the discernment of a Rosh, while Ozen, Hotem, and Peh went out and became a Guf and a vessel of reception for the light of the Einayim. And it was explained above, page 391, the passage beginning “the hairs of his head,” that this great change was not made in the very Rosh of SAG, but in the discernment of the branches that come out from it outward, and that only the discernment of the AHP of the hairs went out and became the discernment of a Guf and a vessel of reception for the light of the Einayim. Study it there well.
And this is what he says: “When the light of the Einayim descends and expands downward through the Akudim, behold, it looks at those lights of AHP.” Its meaning is that the light of the Einayim is bestowed upon and clothes in the discernment of the AHP that are below the Einayim; for a look means bestowal and reception, as is known. And since these AHP receive the light of the Einayim from above downward, they have thereby gone out from the discernment of a Rosh and become the discernment of a Guf. And you already know that they are not the AHP of the Rosh of SAG itself, but only branches of it, which are called the hairs of the Dikna [beard].
And these hairs of the Dikna are likewise discerned as two discernments; for there are necessarily ten Sefirot in them, since they are a complete level called the light of the Einayim. Therefore they too divide into GE and AHP, like their root, from which they came out.
Therefore there are in them three discernments. The first is the AHP in the place of their emergence, which in AA of Atzilut are called the locks of hair beneath the corners of the head, on the right and on the left, below the ears, down to the angles of the cheeks below, from where the Dikna begins to widen; and this is the discernment of the Ozen in the place of its emergence. And the discernment of the Hotem in the place of its emergence is called by the name of the hairs that surround the upper lip on the right and on the left. And the discernment of the Peh in the place of its emergence is called by the name Orcha [path], in the middle of the upper lip beneath the Hotem, which is free of hairs. And all these three corrections of the Dikna are reckoned as the discernment of a Rosh, of the discernment of Galgalta and Einayim alone, and they are the first discernment of the Dikna. And the second discernment is the discernment of the AHP that went outside the Rosh of the Dikna, which in their source are reckoned as the discernment of a Rosh; but for the reason that they are the light of the Einayim, whose law it is that there is in it only GE in the Rosh, while the Ozen, Hotem, and Peh in it are not found in its Rosh but go out to the Guf, as above — from this aspect the second discernment, of the AHP of the Dikna, is reckoned as the discernment of a Guf. And these outer AHP of the Dikna are called the Shibolet [strand] of the beard, which is the fourth correction of the Dikna of AA; they are the hairs that hang upon the lower lip, in the middle of it, and it is discerned as the place of gathering of all three corrections that are in the discernment of GE, which is discerned as the Rosh of the Dikna, as above. And it is called the place of gathering because this Shibolet is the vessel of reception for the lights that are in the Rosh of the Dikna, and all that there is in the Rosh, which are the AHP in the place of their emergence, is bestowed and gathered in this Shibolet. And the third discernment of the Dikna is all the rest of the corrections of the Dikna that are extended down to the Chazeh, that is, until its completion; for they are its true discernment of ZAT, meaning that they are the discernment of a Guf and a vessel of reception even in their source.
And this is what he says: “When the light of the eye descends, it passes through Ozen, Hotem, and Peh, and looks at those lights of AHP.” That is, as above, that the lights of the Einayim are bestowed upon the AHP, and therefore they become the discernment of vessels and receivers, and thereby go out from the discernment of a Rosh to the discernment of a Guf, as above. And this is what he says: “And it takes light from them for the need of making the vessels of the Nekudot,”
meaning that the vessels of Nekudim too, which receive from them, must be according to their quality, as he goes on to explain.
